Rashi on Shabbat 129a:10:2.english: [One who] let blood - And all the more so [for] a sick person.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:11:1.hebrew: צלחו ליה תכתקא דשאגא - לא מצאו עצים מוכנים להיסק ביום הקזה, וצוה ובקעו כסא של תדהר, שהוא מעולה בדמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:11:1.english: They split for him a chair of shaga - They did not find wood prepared for kindling on the day of [his] bloodletting, so he ordered [them] and they split a chair of tidhar [wood], which is of great value.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:11:2.hebrew: פתורא דיונה - מין ארז הוא, ורבינו הלוי אמר בוי"ש:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:11:2.english: A table of yonah - It is a species of cedar, and Rabbeinu HaLevi said [it is] buis [boxwood].

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:11:3.english: [For] Rava, they split a sharshifa for him - A bench.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:13:1.english: And purchase shoes - For there is no [greater] disgrace than one who walks barefoot in the marketplace.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:14:1.english: (What are) the needs of a meal - (the needs of) a bloodletting meal.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:1.english: On the day of the practice - Of bloodletting.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:2.english: Of spleens - Spleen; red in place of red [blood].

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:4.english: From his ears - From his ears [people] smell the wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:5.english: Until his spleen floated - His spleen floated in wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:6.hebrew: מריבדא דכוסילתא - נקבי כלי האומן שבבשרו, פלימ"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:6.english: From the bloodletting incision - The punctures of the bloodletter's instrument in his flesh — *fleme* [Old French for fleam, a bloodletting lancet].

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:7.hebrew: בר תלתא טרפי - בן ג' שנים, שטענה אמו משנקלט ג' עלין חדשין:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:16:7.english: Of three leaves - Three years old, [for] its mother [vine] bore three new leaves since it took root:

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:17:1.english: To the Sages - To his students.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:17:2.english: Say: Nachman happened [to come] to us - Prepare an abundant meal, as if I were dining with you.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:1.english: Except for that artifice - Which he proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:2.english: And it is not possible for him - To buy wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:3.english: Let him take a worn zuz - A bad and inferior zuz that does not circulate in spending.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:4.hebrew: וליזיל לשב חנותא - ודרך הלוקחים לטועמו תחלה שיהא טוב, ויטעום. וכשיתן לו הזוז, והחנווני ימצאנו רע ולא יקבלנו, והוא ילך לחנות אחרת ויעשה כן:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:4.english: And let him go to seven stores - And [it is] the way of buyers to taste [the wine] first [to see] that it is good, and [so] he will taste [some]. And when he gives him the zuz, the storekeeper will find it bad and will not accept it, and he will go to another store and do likewise.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:5.english: And if not - [That is,] he does not have a bad zuz.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:6.hebrew: ולישוף משחא בצידעיה - ברקתו. והתמרים והשומן מחממין אותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:18:6.english: And let him smear oil on his temple - On his temple; and the dates and the oil warm him.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:19:1.hebrew: בישא מי הוה טבא - חום השמש שהוא קשה לאדם, כלום מטיב לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:19:1.english: Does evil become good? - The heat of the sun, which is harmful to a person, does it benefit him at all?

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:1.hebrew: היכא דכריך זיקא - אינדרו"ן שיש בו חלונות, והרוח נכנסת בהם נכרכת ומתגלגלת באינדרו"ן:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:1.english: Where the wind swirls - A chamber that has windows, and the wind entering through them swirls and rolls around in the chamber.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:2.hebrew: דילמא שפי ליה אומנא - מריקו מדמו, כמו השופה יין לחבירו (ב"מ דף ס.):
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:2.english: Perhaps the bloodletter drains him - [meaning] he empties him of his blood, like "one who decants wine for his fellow" (Bava Metzia 60a).

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:3.hebrew: ומוקי ליה ארביעתא - לא הניח בו דם אלא כדי חייו, דהיינו רביעית. והדר אתי ליה זיקא ושייף ליה מדם הנותר בגופו, ומחסרו משיעורו ומסתכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:22:3.english: And establishes him at a quarter [of a log] - [The bloodletter] left no blood in him except enough for his survival, which is a quarter [-log]. Then the wind comes upon him and draws out some of the blood remaining in his body, reducing it below its [minimum] measure, and he is endangered.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:23:1.hebrew: שב לביני ואריחא - עובי החומה ז' לבינים מוטלין לרחבן זה אצל זה, דכל לבינה ג"ט, ואריחא — אריח, חצי לבינה, טפח ומחצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:23:1.english: Seven bricks and an aricha - The thickness of the wall [was] seven bricks laid widthwise, one next to the other, for each brick [is] three handbreadths; and aricha [means] an ariach, half a brick, a handbreadth and a half.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:23:2.english: He felt in himself - He felt in himself that he was weakened.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:23:3.english: One half-brick was lacking - The wall was lacking a half-brick from its thickness.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:2:1.hebrew: בין שאמרה אין צריכה אני - וחברותיה אומרות שהיא צריכה, מחללין:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:2:1.english: Whether she said, "I do not need [it]" - And her companions say that she needs [it], one desecrates [Shabbat for her].

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:4:1.english: By her arms - By her arms, for she is unable to walk.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:6:1.hebrew: חיה ג' ימים וז' ימים ול' יום - הוזכרו בה לחילוק הלכות חילול שבת. ל' מז' עד השלמת ל', וכן ז' מג' עד השלמת ז':
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:6:1.english: A woman in childbirth: three days, and seven days, and thirty days - [These] were mentioned regarding her for the distinction of the laws of desecrating Shabbat. Thirty [days means] from seven until the completion of thirty, and similarly seven [days means] from three until the completion of seven.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:1.hebrew: כל צרכי חולה - והא חיה עד ל' יום, סתמא חולה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:1.english: All needs of a sick person - And this woman who has given birth, up to thirty days [after childbirth], is generally [considered] a sick person.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:2.hebrew: דבר שאין בו סכנה - חולה שאם לא יעשו לו רפואה זו, אין מסוכן למות, ומ"מ צריך הוא לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:2.english: A matter in which there is no danger - [Referring to] a sick person who, if they do not perform this remedy for him, is not in danger of dying, yet nevertheless he needs it.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:3.hebrew: אומר לארמאי ועושה - אבל דבר שיש בו סכנה, ישראל עצמו עושה לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:7:3.english: One says to a gentile and he performs [it] - But [in] a matter in which there is danger, a Jew himself performs [it] for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:8:1.hebrew: לטבילה - עד ל' יום לא תטבול, מפני הצינה:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:8:1.english: With regard to immersion - Until thirty days [have passed], she should not immerse because of the cold.

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:9:1.english: When her husband is not with her - And she immerses for ritually pure [foods].

Rashi on Shabbat 129a:9:2.hebrew: בעלה מחממה - לאחר טבילה בתשמיש, והגוף מתחמם מן הגוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 129a:9:2.english: Her husband warms her - After immersion, through marital relations, and the body is warmed by the [other] body.

Tosafot on Shabbat 129a:5:1.hebrew: רבא משמיה דרב יהודה אמר שבעה - לכאורה משמע דרבא לטעמיה, דבפרק הדר (עירובין דף סח.) גבי ההוא ינוקא דאישתפוך חמימיה, אמר להו רבא: "נישייליה לאימיה, אם צריכה — ניחיימו אגב אימיה". דמסתמא ביום שמיני היה, קודם מילה, שהיה צריך חמין למולו — דלאחר מילה מסוכן הוא, ובלא אימיה ביום שמיני מחללין עליו שבת — והיינו לאחר שבעה, דבנסתם הקבר בעינן "צריכה". מיהו ללישנא דאמרי לה לרבא שלשים, תיקשי למה צריכה! ועוד, דבקונטרס פי' התם: ניחיימו אגב אימיה ע"י נכרי, וכן פירש ר"ח. לכך יש לפרש דאביי ורבא ואמרי לה — מר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי, וכולהו קיימו כנהרדעי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 129a:5:1.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Yehuda: Seven [days] - At first glance, it seems that Rava [follows] his own reasoning [elsewhere], for in the chapter Hadar (Eruvin 68a), regarding that infant whose hot water was spilled, Rava said to them: "Let us ask his mother; if she needs [it], let them heat [water] on account of his mother." For presumably it was on the eighth day, before the circumcision, when he needed hot water to circumcise him — for after circumcision he is in danger, and [even] without his mother we desecrate Shabbat for him on the eighth day — and this [eighth day] is after seven [days], when, once the womb has closed, we require [that] she needs [it]. However, according to the version of "and others say" [attributed] to Rava [that it lasts] thirty [days], it is difficult: why [must] she need [it]? And furthermore, Rashi explained there [that] "let them heat [it] on account of his mother" [means] by means of a gentile, and so too Rabbeinu Chananel explained. Therefore, one should explain that Abaye, Rava, and "and others say" — one stated one [ruling] and one stated another [ruling], and they do not disagree, and all of them are in accordance with [the Sages of] Neharde'a:
